function.name: get_market_regime
function.description: What kind of market this is right now, and -- the important half -- whether a specific buy_below/sell_above band would ever actually fire in it. Pass your candidate thresholds and `band_check` replays them over 30 days of real hourly candles and returns how many buys, sells and completed round trips they would have made, the edge per round trip net of the measured round-trip cost, and a plain verdict: STERILE (buy_below sits below every low in the window, so the strategy would hold cash forever and score exactly its starting balance), ONE-WAY (it buys and can never reach sell_above, so it is buy-and-hold with extra steps), or a round-trip count. CALL THIS BEFORE YOU COMMIT ANY THRESHOLD: on 2026-08-05, 8 of 34 strategies in this population had never placed a single trade -- some after 33 hours -- purely because their band did not intersect the market, and monitor.py now rejects a revision whose backtest replays zero trades. `regime` gives the context (trend, ATR per bar against the round-trip cost, where spot sits in its 30-day range, drawdown from the high) and `suggest_bands` ranks a grid of widths by total net basis points -- read its `note`, it is an in-sample fit and is for ruling widths OUT, not for copying the top row.

hours.description: How much candle history to read. Default 720 (30 days).

buy_below.description: Candidate buy threshold to replay. Omit to skip band_check.

sell_above.description: Candidate sell threshold to replay. Omit to skip band_check.

function.name: get_dex_cex_basis
function.description: Current dislocation between where an asset is quoted on centralized exchanges and where it actually trades on the Stellar DEX order book. Every strategy here decides on price_feed's CEX aggregate but executes against the DEX, so this is the gap between the price you reason about and the price you get. Returns cex_mid, dex_bid/ask/mid, spread_bp, basis_bp (how far the DEX is from the CEX; positive means the DEX is rich, i.e. a good place to sell and a bad place to buy) and tradeable_bp (that gap MINUS the cost of crossing to capture it). Act on tradeable_bp, never on basis_bp alone -- capturing a 3 bp dislocation by crossing a 12 bp book loses money. tradeable_bp is negative most of the time, which is itself the signal: it says when not to trade.

code.description: Asset code, or 'XLM' (the default) for the base leg

issuer.description: The issuer's 56-character G... address. Omit for XLM.

function.name: get_friction
function.description: What trading an asset actually costs: the half-spread charged on one fill and the total for a full buy-then-sell round trip, in basis points. This cost is real and is already charged inside both trade_logger.execute_trade and backtest_strategy, so it is inside every number you are judged on. Use it to check that a threshold band is wider than the cost of the round trip that would capture it -- a band narrower than round_trip_bp cannot be profitable no matter how often it is right. Non-XLM assets are dramatically more expensive than XLM (measured: XLM ~9 bp, AQUA ~151 bp, ARS ~186 bp), so always check before sizing a leg's thresholds.

code.description: Asset code, or 'XLM' (the default) for the base leg

issuer.description: The issuer's 56-character G... address. Omit for XLM.

function.name: get_market_history
function.description: Recorded PER-MINUTE market conditions going back as far as the market recorder daemon has been running: DEX book width (spread_bp), bid/ask depth, the DEX/CEX basis (basis_bp and tradeable_bp) and news sentiment. This is the only persistent history of anything other than price -- ohlc_history covers price alone, and it is a CEX price. Use it to check whether an edge you are about to build survives when the book is wide, or whether the basis mean-reverts on a timescale you could trade. Returns a min/mean/max summary, the recorded span, and a sample of raw rows taken at an even stride across the whole window (not just the tail), with `rows_are` saying which. Note the cadence changed from hourly to per-minute, so a window that spans the change has both.

hours.description: How far back to read, in hours (default 168 = one week)

function.name: backtest_strategy
function.description: Replay a strategy over real historical XLM/USD candles and return return_pct, buy_hold_pct, beats_buy_hold, trades, win_rate and max_drawdown_pct. Use it as your fitness check instead of guessing. beats_buy_hold is computed on the XLM leg ONLY. If the strategy declares extra assets, each is replayed separately over its own (shorter, thinner, gappier) Stellar DEX history and reported under `legs` -- check `active_buckets` there before trusting a leg's return, since a leg with few traded buckets rests on very little real price discovery. Do not over-fit to leg numbers. Always check `decide_source` first: 'main.py:decide' means your code was replayed; 'config-thresholds' means the backtester could not import decide() from main.py and replayed config.json's plain buy_below/sell_above rule instead -- in that case a top-level `WARNING` key is present and every other number describes the config, not the code, so fix main.py's structure and re-run before trusting beats_buy_hold. IF YOUR STRATEGY USES THE DEX/CEX BASIS (state['basis_bp'] / state['basis_tradeable_bp']): the default 30-day hourly replay cannot see it, because the recorded basis series is per-minute and recent. Re-run with interval=1 and days=0.5 for a 12-hour replay on a 1-minute grid, then read basis_coverage (how much of the window had a real recorded basis behind it), basis_edge_excess_bp (how much better your fills were timed against the venue than luck would give) and beats_basis_null. A top-level `BASIS_WARNING` appears when coverage is too low for those to mean anything. Do NOT read beats_buy_hold off a 12-hour run -- half a day of return is half a day of whatever XLM happened to do, not evidence about your logic.

strategy_path.description: Directory of the strategy to test, e.g. /opt/strategies/clone_ab12cd34ef56

days.description: How many days of history to replay (default 30, max useful ~30 at interval=60). Fractional values are allowed and are how you reach a short high-resolution window: days=0.5 with interval=1 is a 12-hour, 1-minute replay.

ticks_per_candle.description: Decision points per candle. 1 (default) evaluates once per hour; pass 120 to approximate the live loop's 30-second polling cadence, which matters for strategies that fire repeatedly while a threshold is standing.

interval.description: Candle size in minutes: 1, 5, 15, 60 (default), 240 or 1440. Use 1 (with days=0.5) to replay basis logic, which mean-reverts far faster than an hourly candle can show. Upstream caps a 1-minute request at ~720 candles, so 12 hours is the ceiling there.

function.name: backtest_forecast_strategy
function.description: Replay a forecasting strategy over a fixed set of resolved questions and return trades, decide_source, mean_brier, mean_base_brier, beats_null and null_pct. Use it as your fitness check instead of guessing -- lower mean_brier is better, and beats_null is true only when your mean_brier is below mean_base_brier (0.25, the score of always guessing 0.5). Always check decide_source first: 'main.py:decide' means your code was replayed; anything else means the backtester could not import decide() from main.py and replayed the mechanical confidence_gain-only fallback instead -- in that case a top-level WARNING key is present and every number describes the fallback, not your code, so fix main.py's structure and re-run before trusting beats_null.

strategy_path.description: Directory of the strategy to test, e.g. /opt/strategies/clone_ab12cd34ef56

n.description: How many fixed historical questions to replay (default 2000). This set is unrelated to the live game's questions, so results are always comparable across runs.

function.name: backtest_kalshi_strategy
function.description: Replay a Kalshi strategy over a fixed set of ALREADY-RESOLVED real Kalshi markets and return trades, decide_source, mean_brier, mean_market_brier, beats_null and null_pct. Use it as your fitness check instead of guessing -- lower mean_brier is better, and beats_null is true only when your mean_brier is below mean_market_brier (what the market's own frozen price would have scored against the real outcome). Always check decide_source first: 'main.py:decide' means your code was replayed; anything else means the backtester could not import decide() from main.py and replayed the mechanical confidence_gain-only fallback instead -- in that case a top-level WARNING key is present and every number describes the fallback, not your code, so fix main.py's structure and re-run before trusting beats_null. Real Kalshi markets are efficiently priced, so beats_null being false is not automatically a failure -- but decide_source must always be 'main.py:decide'.

strategy_path.description: Directory of the strategy to test, e.g. /opt/strategies/clone_ab12cd34ef56

rebuild.description: Force-rebuild the fixed resolved-market set from live Kalshi data before replaying (slow, makes real network calls). Default false reuses the cached set, which is what you want for iterating quickly -- the set is the same for a day at a time regardless.

function.name: get_price_history
function.description: Return recent XLM/USD closing prices as a JSON list, oldest first, from real exchange candles (Kraken with a Coinbase fallback, cached and shared). Use when you want to look at the actual recent trend, volatility, or price range before choosing thresholds or indicator periods -- not the single spot price. Defaults to 720 hourly closes (~30 days).

hours.description: How many hours of history to return (default 720)

function.name: calculate
function.description: Evaluate a basic arithmetic expression (+, -, *, /, **)

function.name: get_current_time
function.description: Get the current local date and time

function.name: get_uptime
function.description: Report system uptime, logged-in user count, and the 1/5/15-minute load averages. Use for any question about system load, how busy the machine is, or how long it has been running.

function.name: read_file
function.description: Read and return the full contents of a file at the given path.

path.description: Absolute or relative path to the file to read

function.name: write_file
function.description: Write content to a file at the given path, creating it if it doesn't exist and overwriting it if it does.

path.description: Absolute or relative path to the file to write

content.description: Text content to write to the file

function.name: fetch_url
function.description: Fetch the contents of a URL via curl (follows redirects) and return the response body.

url.description: The URL to fetch, e.g. https://example.com

function.name: install_package
function.description: Install a package via apt-get (apt-get install -y <package>).

package.description: The apt package name to install, e.g. jq

function.name: update_package_list
function.description: Refresh the apt package index (apt-get update). Run this before installing a package if it might not be found.

function.name: exec
function.description: Execute a shell command via `/bin/sh -c <command>` and return its combined stdout/stderr. Use for anything not covered by a more specific tool (e.g. process management, piping, shell built-ins). Not sandboxed beyond the container itself, so avoid destructive commands.

command.description: The shell command to run, e.g. "ls -la /opt"

function.name: get_news_sentiment
function.description: Current crypto news headlines for an asset plus a keyword-based sentiment score in [-1, 1], where negative is bearish. Use it to decide whether a news filter is worth wiring into a strategy and to sanity-check a veto threshold against what the feed actually reads right now. IMPORTANT: this is a live reading with no history behind it -- there is no headline archive, so backtest_strategy always replays news sentiment as 0.0 (neutral). A news rule therefore cannot be measured by beats_buy_hold; it is judged only by live paper score. In main.py, read it inside decide() as state.get('news_sentiment', 0.0) and let the trading loop fetch it once per tick -- never call the news feed from decide() itself.

asset.description: Asset code to fetch news for; defaults to XLM.

function.name: list_candidate_assets
function.description: List Stellar assets that a strategy could add as one of its up to 2 extra trading legs, ranked by liquidity and reputation. Returns code, issuer, rating, trustline count and 7d volume for each. Use this to FIND candidate assets rather than recalling asset issuers from memory -- an asset code alone is not unique and impostors exist on-chain. Presence in this list is a proposal, not approval: every asset is still re-verified by monitor.py before the strategy starts.

function.name: verify_asset
function.description: Check whether a specific (code, issuer) Stellar asset would be admitted for trading, and see the underlying evidence: reputation rating, trustline count, 7d volume, issuer flags, order-book spread and depth, and any disqualifying concerns. Call this BEFORE writing an asset into config.json -- monitor.py runs the same check and silently deletes any asset that fails.

issuer.description: The issuer's full 56-character G... address. Never abbreviate it and never write one from memory.

function.name: get_asset_price
function.description: Current USD mark for one Stellar asset plus live order-book liquidity (spread, bid depth, ask depth). Use this to set that asset's buy_below/sell_above thresholds against its real current price, and to judge how large a position it could actually support.

function.name: get_asset_price_history
function.description: Hourly OHLC candles for one Stellar asset, oldest first, for computing indicators on an extra asset leg. Note this history comes from Stellar's on-chain DEX and is thinner and gappier than the XLM/USD history from get_price_history -- hours with no trades are absent entirely.

function.name: backtest_maker_strategy
function.description: Replay a market-making strategy over recorded order book snapshots joined to the executed trade tape, and report what its resting quotes would have earned. Use this on every maker revision before committing it. Returns trades (FILLS, not requotes), fill_rate, quote_uptime_pct, spread_captured_usd, adverse_selection_usd and their difference net_edge_usd, inventory_max_usd, return_pct, null_pct and beats_null. Read spread_captured_usd and adverse_selection_usd together -- gross spread capture alone makes every width look profitable. Check decide_source is 'main.py:quote' before trusting any number: anything else means quote() could not be imported and the result describes a fallback, not your code.

strategy_path.description: Absolute path to the strategy directory.

days.description: Days of recorded book and tape to replay. Default 7.

function.name: get_tape_stats
function.description: Executed-trade statistics for XLM/USDC over the last N hours, bucketed by trade size. Answers the sizing questions the order book cannot: how many trades per hour print at or above the size you would quote, how much volume that is, how one-sided the aggressing flow has been (taker_buy_pct), and what share was liquidity-pool flow no resting offer could have captured. Note the flow is roughly balanced over a week but wildly one-sided over any single hour, so do not calibrate an inventory rule on a short window.
